Please take a moment to rest before you continue.

Click "Continue" for the next part.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

In this task, we will show you problems that people sometimes have. They will appear on the screen two at a time. When you see them, take a moment to reflect, and think about how often each of these problems has bothered you in the last two weeks. Your task is to compare them and click on the problem that bothered you more.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

Sometimes the difference between the two problems might seem very small. Still, we ask that you think about the last two weeks, and try your best to choose the problem that bothered you more.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

For some pairs, you may find that you have not experienced either problem. If so, you can click on a "Neither bothered me" button to report that neither of the two problems affected you during the past two weeks. However, remember that the problems presented are common and experienced by most people to some extent. Please try to use the "Neither bothered me" button only when you are absolutely sure neither problem affected you at all.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

The task includes 105 screens in total. To make it easier, it is divided into four smaller parts of approximately 25 screens each. Overall, it should take about 20-30 minutes. There is no time limit, so please take your time to carefully reflect on each screen.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

You will have three built-in breaks during the task. This gives you a chance to take a short, refreshing pause between each of the four parts.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

During the task, please stay focused on this screen. Switching to other tabs or windows is not allowed, so please keep the task open and in front of you until you reach the very end.

Part 2 - Task Instructions

Our goal is to understand exactly how much each problem affected you over the past two weeks compared to all the others. Please do your best to choose the answers that truly reflect your experience. We will now ask you to briefly explain the task in your own words, followed by a short quiz to make sure these instructions are clear. You can go back and review any previous page before starting. Thank you.

As part of the questionnaire, you were asked about how you've been feeling lately, including whether you've had any thoughts of death or suicide.

Some people going through depression also experience thoughts of death or suicide. These thoughts can be frightening, but they are a recognized symptom of depression, and help is available.

Depression can affect anyone, regardless of age, background, culture, or life circumstances.

If you (or someone you know) have been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, irritable, or guilty, struggling with sleep, appetite, concentration, or everyday functioning, or having thoughts of death or suicide — please don't try to manage it alone. Consider reaching out to a psychologist, physician, or mental health professional.

If you are having thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life, please act now:

  • Talk to a family member or friend who can support you.
  • Contact a crisis helpline. You can find a helpline in your country, available free and often 24/7, at: https://findahelpline.com/
